 CLYDE, N.C. (WLOS) — Volunteers at Wider Circle Pigeon River Cooperative are preparing meals for neighbors in need. The Clyde program began after Helene and has now served more than 100,000 meals, according to the organization.
 Wider Circle serves hot meals Tuesday through Saturday, noon to 6 p.m., at Clyde Central United Methodist Church, located at 410 Charles Street. Meals are available to eat in or take out.
 Volunteer Jerry Evans said the meals make a difference for people who have little else.
 "It means a whole lot to somebody that don't have anything," Evans said. "And there's a lot of people that really need this."
 AS SNAP ENROLLMENT DROPS, WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA FOOD PANTRIES SEE SURGE IN DEMAND 
 The program serves more than 300 meals a day, and ministry director Denise Teague said demand is growing. She said people are worried about changes to public benefits, including the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), and unsure how to navigate them.
 "It's a scary time because people have been counting on the SNAP benefits and on their Medicaid to be able to survive," Teague said.
 For people who don't qualify for food benefits, Teague said, community meal programs can offer another place to turn.
 "People are scared, people are unsure what's going to happen, and trying to figure out how to navigate and how to move through," she said. "We're trying our best to gear up for that." Teague said the program will need more food and volunteers if demand continues to rise. Wider Circle says it has received a matching grant that could help raise up to $20,000 through mid-December.
 "Without community support, our friends and neighbors without SNAP benefits will suffer, and so will our community at large," Teague said.
